notes: Anchored corpus for PolyDiff proto-family rediscovery + synthetic regressions.
Witnesses are pinned by SHA-256 ONLY. NO payload bytes appear in this repo.

Anchors cover four canonical proto divergence shapes: field_unknown_count divergence (MEDIUM-HIGH; gogo-protobuf vs google-protobuf unknown-field-handling class), oneof_active_field divergence (MEDIUM-HIGH; oneof-ambiguity class), decode_outcome divergence (HIGH; FlatBuffer offset overflow producing ok vs parse_error), and decoded_field_summary divergence (MEDIUM; msgpack ext-type collision class).
Per-case `implementations` lists the two wrapper ids the case is designed to disagree on; the diff engine runs ALL declared wrappers and picks up these axes (plus any others that surface).
Per-case `expected_fact_vector_diff` is keyed by axis name; each value is a 2-element array of the two impls' observations (matches the `implementations` ordering).

cases.summary: A protobuf wire payload with extra fields not declared in the decoder's schema. google-protobuf and gogo-protobuf historically diverge on the field_unknown_count reported — google-protobuf preserves them in an unknown-fields buffer while gogo-protobuf with certain options strips them silently. When the SMA round-trips the payload, the extra fields may be lost. SHA-256-pinned synthetic representation.
cases.limitations: witness bytes are NOT in this repo; pinned-hash anchor only. The expected fact-vector diff documents the canonical disagreement shape — actual decoder outputs depend on the pinned wrapper versions and on whether gogo-protobuf is available (the stub returns binary_missing in the Python devcontainer, which the diff engine treats as a parse_error divergence rather than the documented unknown-field divergence).

cases.summary: A protobuf wire payload where the same bytes resolve to different active fields in a `oneof` group depending on the decoder's interpretation order. Same payload, different oneof_active_field. Maps to a oneof-ambiguity bug class. SHA-256-pinned synthetic representation.
cases.limitations: synthetic case of our design exercising the oneof_active_field divergence triage rule; oneof-ambiguity has been documented in protobuf spec discussions.

cases.summary: A FlatBuffer payload with an offset value that exceeds the buffer length. flatc with bounds-checking enabled rejects it (parse_error) while a more permissive decoder silently decodes garbage memory. Same payload, ok vs parse_error decode_outcome. Maps to a flatbuffer-offset-overflow bug class (HIGH triage). SHA-256-pinned synthetic representation.
cases.limitations: synthetic case of our design exercising the decode_outcome divergence (ok + parse_error) triage rule on a FlatBuffer offset-overflow shape; the FlatBuffer-cross-decoder pairing here is illustrative — in practice the second wrapper would be a different FlatBuffer impl, but flatc vs protoc_python suffices to surface the decode_outcome divergence axis.

cases.summary: An msgpack payload using an ext-type tag that two decoders interpret differently — e.g. as a timestamp vs raw bytes. Same payload, different decoded_field_summary. Maps to an msgpack-ext-type-collision bug class. SHA-256-pinned synthetic representation.
cases.limitations: synthetic case of our design exercising the decoded_field_summary divergence triage rule on an msgpack ext-type collision shape; the cross-decoder pairing is illustrative (msgpack vs protobuf) — in practice the second wrapper would be a different msgpack impl.
